messages.author: 96f8480d319e302c
messages.subject: Re: Calibfit
parts:
Well, this is indeed problematic.

How do you expect to assign birds without information on sedentary individuals?
This is not an IsoriX issue, but I think a general requirement to perform any assignments using any method (isotope based or not).

Some people do use calibration published by others, so your way out would be to have access to such datasets.
You need, ideally, isotopic data from the same species, in the same physiological state, with the same ages, sampled at the same time as when you bird took off, and from the same areas than your candidate areas.
You also need several data point per locations.
Those data should also have been measured in the same fashion in the lab (same protocol, same isotopes, same standard...).
The more you depart from this ideal situation, the further from the truth your assignment will be.

It is difficult to collect or get such data, but calibration is the bread and butter of assignments.

Le samedi 8 janvier 2022 à 19:03:57 UTC+1, alexandre...@gmail.com a écrit :
Well, this is indeed problematic.

How do you expect to assign birds without information on sedentary individuals?
This is not an IsoriX issue, but I think a general requirement to perform any assignments using any method (isotope based or not).

Some people do use calibration published by others, so your way out would be to have access to such datasets.
You need, ideally, isotopic data from the same species, in the same physiological state, with the same ages, sampled at the same time as when you bird took off, and from the same areas than your candidate areas.
You also need several data point per locations.
Those data should also have been measured in the same fashion in the lab (same protocol, same isotopes, same standard...).
The more you depart from this ideal situation, the further from the truth your assignment will be.

It is difficult to collect or get such data, but calibration is the bread and butter of assignments.
